column1: # evidence_types.tsv — Axis 1 of the two-axis evidence model (PLAN.md J.3): the KIND of
# observation an `evidence_item` records. This is orthogonal to Axis 2 ("support": how many
# independent publications/groups/organisms/condition classes agree), which is not a fixed
# vocabulary and is not listed here.
# `assertion.level` (L1-L5) is a DERIVED view computed from these evidence types plus support
# (PLAN.md J.3) — it is never stored or hand-assigned. `required_fields` is the set enforced by a
# CHECK constraint on the `evidence_item` row of that type (PLAN.md J.3): "a row that lies about
# what kind of evidence it is cannot be written." The `ai_inference` row is the one that matters
# most: it is structurally prevented from carrying a `measurement_id`, so a model's guess can never
# be mistaken for a measured fact downstream.
# `eco_mapping` (Evidence and Conclusion Ontology code) is left NULL (empty) throughout: PLAN.md
# J.3 says mapping to ECO is recorded per evidence item so the atlas can export into the wider
# ecosystem, but does not name specific ECO codes, and this curator is not confident enough in a
# from-memory ECO code to assert one here — left NULL (never recorded) rather than guessed, per
# docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md "Identifiers" (an unresolved identifier is never mapped to the
# nearest plausible match).
# Columns:
#   evidence_type      the closed vocabulary value (PLAN.md J.1 `evidence[]` / J.3 Axis 1)
#   meaning            one-line description of the observation kind
#   required_fields    pipe-separated fields a row of this type must carry (PLAN.md J.3), enforced
#                      by CHECK constraint at the schema layer, not by this vocabulary file itself
#   forbidden_fields   fields a row of this type must NOT carry, or 'NA' if none are singled out
#   eco_mapping        Evidence and Conclusion Ontology code, or empty (NULL) — not yet assigned
#   evidence, confidence   per docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md "Curation"
# Evidence-honesty pass (this revision, following the compartments.tsv D1 rewrite): every row
# below that was 'high' solely on the strength of citing another fermdb file (PLAN.md,
# docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md, a source module, or another vocabulary TSV) has been changed to
# 'unverified' -- citing an internal document is citing memory with an extra hop, not an
# independent check. A row stays 'high' only when its evidence names something actually checked
# outside the repo in this session (e.g. a ChEBI lookup via web search). The confidence vocabulary
# is closed and has four values everywhere ('unverified', 'low', 'medium', 'high'; D2);
# 'unverified' means asserted but never checked against a source, distinct from 'low' (checked,
# weak).
evidence_type
direct_perturbation
column2: The gene/pathway was changed and the product/phenotype measured against a proper control.
column6: PLAN.md J.3 (Axis 1 table and the per-type required-fields table)

column1: direct_biochemical
column2: Enzyme assay, in vitro reconstitution, isotope tracing, or flux measurement.

column1: correlative_omics
column2: Differential expression, proteomics, or co-expression — an association, not a perturbation.

column1: comparative_genomic
column2: A variant or gene's presence associated across strains.

column1: computational_model
column2: FBA, kinetic model, structure or sequence prediction — no wet-lab observation.

column1: literature_assertion
column2: Stated in a paper without primary data shown (e.g. a review or introduction sentence).

column1: ai_inference
column2: Produced by a model within this system, not by an experiment.
column6: PLAN.md J.3: "an AI inference is structurally prevented from masquerading as a measurement." This row is the reason the vocabulary exists as data: any loader must reject an ai_inference row that carries a measurement_id.
